_comment: Examples under datrix/examples/ that the REAL generation pipeline cannot build today.
This is a DELIBERATELY MAINTAINED SCOPE BOUNDARY, not an auto-heal: it converts a genuine,
pre-existing generation FAILURE into a loudly-reported skip in the reference-example parity
gate (datrix/scripts/test/reference-example-parity-gate.ps1). It never hides output drift --
a listed (example, language) pair that does generate is still hash-compared against its baseline.
KEY FORMAT (language sweep): a bare example_id applies to every registered
language the gate sweeps -- for a failure at config-resolution/deployment-plan-building time,
before any language-specific codegen stage runs (the original two entries below). An
'example_id::language' key applies to that one language only -- for a defect in one language's
own codegen stage while the same example generates fine in every other registered language
(a distinction that could not exist before the language sweep made every example genuinely
All entries reproduce with the sanctioned generator (generate.ps1 <system.dtrx> <out> -L <language>),
so none is a gate artifact.
expected_count is a pinned, reviewed value: change it only in the same change that adds or
removes an entry. Removing an entry means the defect is FIXED and the example must be blessed.

examples.03-domains-finance::typescript: Re-verified 2026-08-01, independently of the sweep's prior capture: tsc still fails with TS2367 (no overlap) comparing account['status'], typed as the cross-service response enum AccountServiceAccountStatus, against the DSL's raw string literal 'active' (3 call sites, transaction_api.controller.ts:92,165,168; DSL source examples/03-domains/finance/transaction-service.dtrx:357,395,399). Read the generated clients/account-service-responses.ts: aliasing to the shared AccountStatus enum (the sweep's DSL-level attempt) is not just blocked by nominal typing, it is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE -- this file is deliberately a 'dependency-prefixed' model, self-contained per CONSUMING service, because finance_transaction_service and the producing AccountService are separate deployable TypeScript packages with no build-time import path to each other's source. AccountServiceAccountStatus is finance_transaction_service's OWN generated copy of the enum (class-name rule: {DependencyPascal}{OriginalEnumName}, in _response_struct_context.py's _enum_class_name), not an alias target. The real fix is at the STRING-LITERAL comparison site: the generator must resolve which locally-generated cross-service enum a compared field belongs to (from the field's cross-service response interface, already known to response_struct_generator.py at struct-build time) and coerce the literal to THAT enum's member (AccountServiceAccountStatus.Active), not the shared enum. Requires threading a per-file (interface-name, field-name) -> generated-enum-name table from response-struct generation into visit_binary_op/visit_property_access -- not attempted further within this retest's scope. Same root cause as hr-platform::typescript and real-estate::typescript below.
